title: Arteries of the sole of the foot (plantar)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender, with surface detail added by an image model.

rows: Popliteal artery, at the lower border of popliteus. It is the larger end branch.

Runs down the back of the leg under soleus with the tibial nerve, then passes behind the medial malleolus under the flexor retinaculum, between the tendons of flexor digitorum longus and flexor hallucis longus. There it divides into the medial and lateral plantar arteries.
Posterior compartment of the leg, the tibia, and the sole of the foot. Through the fibular artery it also supplies the lateral compartment.
hy: Its pulse is felt behind the medial malleolus, between the malleolus and the calcaneal tendon. It is checked, together with the dorsalis pedis pulse, when peripheral arterial disease is suspected.

rows: Posterior tibial artery, under the flexor retinaculum behind the medial malleolus. It is the smaller of its two end branches.
Runs forward along the medial side of the sole between abductor hallucis and flexor digitorum brevis.
Muscles of the great toe and skin of the medial side of the sole.
Posterior tibial artery, under the flexor retinaculum behind the medial malleolus. It is the larger of its two end branches.
Runs forward and laterally across the sole to the base of the fifth metatarsal bone, then turns medially, deep in the sole, as the deep plantar arch.
Muscles and skin of the lateral side of the sole.
Lateral plantar artery, of which it is the continuation. It is completed medially by the deep plantar artery, from the dorsalis pedis artery.
Runs across the bases of the metatarsal bones, deep in the sole.
Gives the four plantar metatarsal arteries and perforating branches to the dorsum of the foot.
Run forward in the spaces between the metatarsal bones, on the plantar side of the interossei muscles.
Each runs on as a common plantar digital artery. Perforating branches join the dorsal metatarsal arteries.
Plantar metatarsal arteries, as their continuation near the heads of the metatarsal bones.
Run forward to the webs between the toes.
Each divides into two proper plantar digital arteries.
Mostly the common plantar digital arteries. The artery to the lateral side of the little toe comes directly from the lateral plantar artery.
Run along the two sides of the plantar surface of each toe.
Skin, joints, and tendon sheaths of the plantar side of each toe.
